g.text: fig 8 — channel-independence: one backbone, M different attention maps

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #898781

g.text: each series is its own sample, so each produces its own N×N map. a channel-mixing model must force one shared pattern on all of them.

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #898781

g.text: one 42 × 42 attention map per channel · darker = more weight · channels 0 and 1 are near-duplicates, channel 5 is noise

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #898781

g.text: attention here uses Wᵠ = Wᴷ = I, so a map is exactly patch-shape similarity: the mechanism is shown, not a trained model's learned attention.
